chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Musa al-Kamandani narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ubayd, from Ubayd ibn Harun. He said: Abu Yazid narrated to us from Husayn, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said:
In the month of Ramadan, betake to much seeking of forgiveness and supplication. As for supplication, it will repel calamity from you; and as for seeking forgiveness, it will erase your sins.

key_terms.الاستغفار: Seeking forgiveness (Istighfar) — repeated prayer for divine pardon that erases sins
key_terms.الدعاء: Supplication (Du'a) — personal prayer to Allah that repels calamity
key_terms.شهر رمضان: The month of Ramadan — the sacred fasting month in which these acts are especially efficacious

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the importance of supplication and seeking forgiveness during Ramadan?
ai.summary: In this concise yet powerful exhortation from Imam Ali, narrated during the assembly of the eighth of Ramadan 367 AH, the Commander of the Faithful instructs believers to dedicate themselves to two essential spiritual acts during Ramadan: istighfar (seeking forgiveness) and du'a (supplication). He explains the distinct function of each — supplication serves as a shield against calamity, while seeking forgiveness purifies the soul by erasing sins. This dual prescription highlights Ramadan as a month uniquely suited for spiritual renewal.
